title: ‘Studies for’: A Human-AI Co-Creative Sound Artwork Using a Real-time Multi-channel Sound Generation Model
venue: 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025) Creative AI Track
extended_summary:
This paper presents a case study of a collaborative AI-assisted sound artwork, Studies for, created with sound artist Evala. The work is motivated by the difficulty of archiving site-specific and performative sound art, where the original experience depends on time, place, and spatialized audio conditions that are difficult to preserve in conventional archives. The authors propose a “new form of archive” in which an AI model trained on an artist’s prior works can continue generating new outputs that remain stylistically faithful while still introducing novelty.

The intervention is a real-time, multi-channel generative sound system based on SpecMaskGIT. The model was trained exclusively on approximately 200 hours of Evala’s past sound artworks and conditioned using both audio and text prompts derived from the artist’s prior work. The system was optimized for fast, continuous eight-channel generation at 48 kHz so it could run throughout a three-month exhibition in Tokyo. Artist feedback was incorporated iteratively to preserve the artist’s identity in the outputs and avoid outputs that were merely collages of prior pieces.

The paper is not an educational study and does not involve students or teachers. Instead, it reports an art-and-technology deployment in an exhibition setting with an adult public audience. The authors conclude that lightweight, fast generative models can support iterative human-AI co-creation, preserve artistic style, and enable continuous generation over long periods. They also argue that multi-modal conditioning can help produce outputs that are both faithful to the artist and sufficiently surprising to be creatively useful.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A general generative AI / text-to-audio model used for real-time generative synthesis rather than a specific named consumer product.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper studies SpecMaskGIT, a lightweight text-to-audio generative model, as the core AI system for co-creating and continuously generating sound in the artwork Studies for.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a creative AI system paper describing the design and implementation of a generative sound installation, not an empirical education study. It does not evaluate instructional coaching, lesson-plan feedback, or K–12 outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational intervention outcomes are reported, and there is no measured impact on learners or teachers. The paper focuses on artistic workflow and system design rather than instructional effectiveness or harm.
